subject: Hyperlane dedicated pool: GPU mix, perf/$ structure and committed tiers
messages:
From: Ava Summers <ava.summers@hyperlane.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@hyperlane.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hyperlane RFP: initial usage + GPU preferences

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick intro call yesterday. Attached is a condensed RFP and our current 6‑month forecast (Hyperlane_RFP_GPU_Usage.xlsx). High level:
- Steady-state concurrency: ~120 concurrent inference streams, avg seq len ~1.2k tokens.
- Burst profile: occasional spikes to ~280 concurrent for 10–30m (market events).
- Model family: a tuned LLM distributed as two variants — a quality-sensitive variant (~2B tokens/day) and a low-cost variant (~6B tokens/day) for lightweight requests.

Our procurement team is evaluating committed reserved capacity (Dedicated pools) with priority on:
1) predictable perf/$ (p95 latency targets)
2) memory headroom for large-batch KV caches (we saw benefits on A100 80GB)
3) discounting tied to committed vCPU/GPU months rather than pure usage credits

We currently prefer H100 for the high-throughput inference path but are open to a mixed fleet if it materially improves cost. Can you sketch a couple of packaging options (pure H100, A100-80GB heavy, and a mixed L40S burst band) and include perf/$ numbers and any tradeoffs around latency SLOs?

Also attaching a short SOW template (SOW_draft_Hyperlane.docx) — procurement will want SLA language and ramp windows.

Best,
Ava Summers
Head of Platform Partnerships
Hyperlane AI

Attachments: Hyperlane_RFP_GPU_Usage.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Summers <ava.summers@hyperlane.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperlane RFP: initial usage + GPU preferences

Hi Ava — thanks for the file and the clear ask. Quick read-through below and a short plan for follow-up.

Summary takeaways from our side:
- Baseline fit: your steady-state and burst profile is a textbook candidate for a committed Dedicated pool with a two-tier fleet: H100s (for quality-sensitive streams) + L40S for cost-efficient, high-concurrency lightweight requests.
- Perf/$: ballpark (tokenized throughput per $): H100 > A100 (higher perf, higher $/GPU), L40S delivers the best $/token for short context ops but has smaller KV/memory headroom.

We’ll produce a 3-option proposal: 1) H100-heavy (SLA-backed p95), 2) A100‑80GB (memory-first), 3) Hybrid H100+L40S (cost-balanced with burst routing). Each option will include: committed-month tiers, baseline throughput guarantees (tokens/sec and p95 latency targets), and suggested canary rollout plan.

Next steps: I’ll send a draft pricing packet + perf matrix by EOD (attached as redwood_dedicated_pricing_v4.pdf). Kimberly, can you confirm if Hyperlane requires KMS/HSM proofs in the first contract? That will affect Private vs Dedicated packaging as well.

—
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555‑0193

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v4.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
From: Hyperlane Procurement <procurement@hyperlane.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperlane RFP: committed tiers and SLA expectations

Markus / Kimberly — following up with procurement specifics and the SOW. Two things procurement highlighted:
1) We need explicit throughput guarantees for both steady and burst states (p95 and p99 targets) with credits for missed SLOs.
2) We prefer a commit structure tied to GPU-months with an annualized minimum — three tiers under consideration: 12 GPU‑mo, 36 GPU‑mo, 72 GPU‑mo.

Also included is a redline to the SOW (attached). A few clarifying Qs:
- For mixed fleets, can you guarantee automatic routing rules so that quality-sensitive requests are pinned to H100 during contention?
- For canary: we need a 30–60 day performance trial with clear rollback if latency/regression thresholds are hit.
- Discounts: procurement expects discounts to be anchored to the committed GPU‑months and to increase at higher tiers — they expect an initial econ model (perf/$) that makes the 36+ GPU‑month tiers compelling.

Attached: SOW_draft_Hyperlane_redline.docx (redlines, 14KB)

Cheers,
Ethan Cole
Procurement Manager
Hyperlane AI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hyperlane RFP: negotiation posture + pricing model thoughts

Markus / Marissa / Neha — forwarding procurement note. My read: prioritize a clear, tiered GPU‑month commit that shows stepwise perf/$ improvements and build in a burst pool (L40S) for microbursts to avoid paying H100 rates for short windows. Proposed quick counter-offer structure (internal):

- Option A (Premium): 100% H100 (SLA: p95 <= 80ms on target models), committed tiers: 12 / 36 / 72 GPU‑mo. Discount schedule: 12 => 8% off list, 36 => 18%, 72 => 28%. Add-on: 10% extra discount if signed on annual prepay.
- Option B (Memory-first): A100-80GB primary for large KV cache workloads, tiers: 12 / 36 / 72, discounts: 12=>6%, 36=>14%, 72=>22%. Note: better KV stability but 10–15% lower perf/$ on generation.
- Option C (Hybrid): H100 for quality tier + L40S ring for burst and high-concurrency ops. Tiers commit expressed as H100-equivalent GPU-months (mix factor). Discounts: 12=>7%, 36=>17%, 72=>26%. Can include an automatic routing policy: priority pinning to H100 for quality traffic, overflow to L40S with graceful latency degradation and documented fallbacks.

We should avoid deep commit language tied to token counts; insist on GPU-month commitments but offer rolling true-up usage credits. Also recommend a 45‑day canary (compromise on their 30–60 day ask) with defined regression metrics.

Marissa — can you prepare the perf/$ delta table (H100 vs A100 vs L40S) for the deck? Neha — confirm whether the standard SLA credit language (monthly credit based on missed p95) is acceptable or procurement needs a different metric.

K

—
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Summers <ava.summers@hyperlane.ai>, Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@hyperlane.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hyperlane committed tiers + proposal (draft)

Ava / Ethan — thanks for the clarity and the redline. Attached is our formal proposal and a short perf matrix. Highlights below: 

1) Packaging options (summary):
- Premium H100: target p95 <= 75–85ms (model dependent), recommended for quality tier. Perf/$: baseline coefficient 1.0 (reference).
- A100-80GB: best for large KV caches (memory-heavy), p95 ~90–120ms, perf/$ ~0.88 vs H100.
- Hybrid (H100 + L40S burst): H100 handles quality traffic; L40S handles lightweight requests and burst overflow. Perf/$ improves ~1.12x on cost for overall workload in your forecast due to L40S handling 60% of requests by volume.

2) Commit structure (GPU-months):
- Tiers: 12 / 36 / 72 GPU-months (can be expressed as committed H100-equivalent; hybrid mixes use conversion factors in appendix).
- Proposed discounts (applied to list GPU-month rate):
  * 12 GPU-mo: 7%
  * 36 GPU-mo: 17%
  * 72 GPU-mo: 26%
- Additional 8% one-time prepay discount for annual upfront payment (applies after tier discount).

3) Throughput & SLOs:
- Steady-state p95 targets included per model; p99 targets in appendix. Latency credits: monthly credit of 5% of committed spend per missed SLO bucket, escalating if repeated for two consecutive months.
- Canary: 45-day performance trial with automatic rollback if p95 regressions >12% vs baseline in two measured windows.

4) Routing & fallbacks:
- Automatic policy: requests flagged as quality-sensitive (header-based) are pinned to H100; overflow routed to L40S. We will document deterministic routing rules in the SOW and provide tracing hooks in Console for the canary.

5) Next actions:
- I’ve attached redwood_dedicated_pricing_v4.pdf and SOW_draft_Hyperlane.docx with the conversion appendix. Please review and we can sync on Friday for a 30‑minute contract walk through. If this looks good, we’ll prepare a DocuSign SOW for signature and propose a target start of 2026-11-01 for the canary.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
